Three questions to start with

Put these to the developer in writing. Each says who should answer and what a good answer looks like.

  1. Q1 Ask the legal team, before booking

    The registration names Nayan Real Estate Private Limited as promoter, while the project is sold as Hubtown. Which company signs my agreement for sale, issues my receipts and holds the title? Please give its CIN and registered office in writing.

    Why it matters. You can only enforce your agreement against the company that signs it. A brand creates no obligation.

    A good answer
    A signed letter naming one company with its CIN, matching the RERA certificate and the draft agreement.
    Does not close it
    "It is all Hubtown" or a group chart in a brochure.

    Where it appears: aurumproptech.in / mumbai-city/hubtown-celeste-P51900008925

  2. Q2 Ask the promoters, before booking

    Hubtown's Managing Director and a Hubtown director appear on Nayan Real Estate's filing. Will Hubtown Limited sign an enforceable guarantee of completion and of Nayan's obligations under my agreement, including refunds and delay interest?

    Why it matters. Common control is not legal liability. Without a signed guarantee the listed parent owes you nothing if the project company fails.

    A good answer
    A guarantee or undertaking executed by Hubtown Limited and annexed to the agreement, reviewed by your lawyer.
    Does not close it
    A verbal assurance or a press release.

    Where it appears: aurumproptech.in / mumbai-city/hubtown-celeste-P51900008925, tofler.in / company/L45200MH1989PLC050688, bseindia.com / AttachHis/feef6693-193f-4cab-b381-360a67521ede.pdf

  3. Q3 Ask the legal team, before booking

    The project was registered in August 2017 and its filed completion date is 31 July 2029. What was the original completion date, how many times has it been extended, and did the existing allottees consent to each extension as MahaRERA requires?

    Why it matters. Twelve years from registration to completion is long. Each extension, and whether buyers consented, shows how the project has been run and what your date is worth.

    A good answer
    The original certificate, every extension order and the allottee-consent records.
    Does not close it
    "Covid delays" without the orders.

    Where it appears: aurumproptech.in / mumbai-city/hubtown-celeste-P51900008925, thelawsuits.in / p=3169

Start here: the questions that matter most

Eight to put first. The full wording, the closing test and a place to track each are in "Every question, by stage".

  1. Q1 Ask the legal team, before booking

    The registration names Nayan Real Estate Private Limited as promoter, while the project is sold as Hubtown. Which company signs my agreement for sale, issues my receipts and holds the title? Please give its CIN and registered office in writing.

    You can only enforce your agreement against the company that signs it. A brand creates no obligation.

  2. Q2 Ask the promoters, before booking

    Hubtown's Managing Director and a Hubtown director appear on Nayan Real Estate's filing. Will Hubtown Limited sign an enforceable guarantee of completion and of Nayan's obligations under my agreement, including refunds and delay interest?

    Common control is not legal liability. Without a signed guarantee the listed parent owes you nothing if the project company fails.

  3. Q3 Ask the legal team, before booking

    The project was registered in August 2017 and its filed completion date is 31 July 2029. What was the original completion date, how many times has it been extended, and did the existing allottees consent to each extension as MahaRERA requires?

    Twelve years from registration to completion is long. Each extension, and whether buyers consented, shows how the project has been run and what your date is worth.

  4. Q4 Ask the sales team, before booking

    Your agents advertise December 2027 as the RERA possession date and March 2027 as a target, but the record shows 31 July 2029. Please confirm in writing which date my agreement will carry.

    Only the date in your registered agreement gives you a remedy; an advertised date gives none.

  5. Q5 Ask the sales team, before booking

    Four sales were registered between July 2025 and June 2026 for about ₹6 crore in total, roughly ₹1.5 crore each, while 1 BHK asking prices start at ₹1.99–2.14 crore. What explains the difference, and what discounts, payment schemes or bulk deals have been offered?

    Registered prices are the market's real evidence; a wide gap to the asking price is leverage in your negotiation, or a sign of special deals you should know about.

  6. Q6 Ask the sales team, before booking

    A RERA-data page reports 19.43% of 211 units booked. How many are sold today, how many to related parties or investors in bulk, and how many remain?

    Slow sales mean less buyer money for construction; bulk sales to insiders can depress resale and voting in the society.

  7. Q7 Ask the promoters, before booking

    The promoter's filing lists one past project, Hubtown Sunmist B wing. Which projects has Nayan Real Estate itself delivered, and which projects run by the same promoters were delivered after their RERA dates?

    The selling company's own delivery record matters more than the brand's.

  8. Q8 Ask the promoters, before booking

    In February 2026 MahaRERA ordered Rare Townships Private Limited to pay delay interest on a Ghatkopar project with no occupation certificate, and Hubtown's results release refers to 72.22% of Rare Townships. What is Hubtown's relationship to that company, and has the order been complied with?

    How the group treats delayed buyers elsewhere is the best evidence of how it would treat you.

Common control, strong link

Nayan Real Estate Private Limited and Hubtown Limited appear to be under common control (4 links). Control is not the same as legal liability: whether Hubtown Limited will stand behind Nayan Real Estate Private Limited's obligations is a question for the developer.

Redevelopment link, possible link

Celeste appears to be connected to a rehabilitation or redevelopment scheme: the registered land adjoins "Rehab 3 Building" and the promoter's address is in that rehab building. If so, the sale building's completion may depend on the rehab obligations.

  1. The record's western boundary is "Adjoining Rehab 3 Building" aurumproptech.in / mumbai-city/hubtown-celeste-P51900008925

Group structure, possible link

Nayan Real Estate looks like one of a pair of Hubtown promoter companies incorporated together, of which only the other is being merged into the listed company. That would leave Celeste's seller outside Hubtown's balance sheet.

  1. Nitant Real Estate Private Limited, named by Hubtown as a merging promoter entity, holds CIN U70102MH2010PTC205729 zaubacorp.com / NITANT-REAL-ESTATE-PRIVATE-LIMITED/U70102MH2010PTC205729, bseindia.com / AttachHis/feef6693-193f-4cab-b381-360a67521ede.pdf
  2. Unverified online reports give Nayan Real Estate's CIN as U70102MH2010PTC205728, the adjacent number (not confirmed by us)
  3. Nayan Real Estate is not named among the merging entities in the part of the FY26 release seen bseindia.com / AttachHis/feef6693-193f-4cab-b381-360a67521ede.pdf

Group delivery record, possible link

A company that Hubtown's own release associates with a 72.22% figure, Rare Townships, was ordered by MahaRERA in February 2026 to pay delay interest on a Mumbai project that had no occupation certificate years after its date.

  1. MahaRERA partly allowed complaints against Rare Townships Private Limited over a Ghatkopar project due by 31 Dec 2022 with the Covid extension freepressjournal.in / mumbai/mumbai-real-estate-dispute-maharera-sets-aside-f…
  2. Hubtown's FY26 results release refers to 72.22% of Rare Townships Private Limited bseindia.com / AttachHis/feef6693-193f-4cab-b381-360a67521ede.pdf

Price, possible link

Registered sale values average about ₹1.5 crore per unit, roughly a quarter below the lowest 1 BHK asking price seen (₹1.99 crore). The registered sales may differ in size or timing, so the buyer should ask for the price history.

Every question, by stage

Before booking

  1. Q1 Ask the legal team, before booking

    The registration names Nayan Real Estate Private Limited as promoter, while the project is sold as Hubtown. Which company signs my agreement for sale, issues my receipts and holds the title? Please give its CIN and registered office in writing.

    Why it matters. You can only enforce your agreement against the company that signs it. A brand creates no obligation.

    A good answer
    A signed letter naming one company with its CIN, matching the RERA certificate and the draft agreement.
    Does not close it
    "It is all Hubtown" or a group chart in a brochure.

    Where it appears: aurumproptech.in / mumbai-city/hubtown-celeste-P51900008925

    Asked Answered Document in hand

  2. Q2 Ask the promoters, before booking

    Hubtown's Managing Director and a Hubtown director appear on Nayan Real Estate's filing. Will Hubtown Limited sign an enforceable guarantee of completion and of Nayan's obligations under my agreement, including refunds and delay interest?

    Why it matters. Common control is not legal liability. Without a signed guarantee the listed parent owes you nothing if the project company fails.

    A good answer
    A guarantee or undertaking executed by Hubtown Limited and annexed to the agreement, reviewed by your lawyer.
    Does not close it
    A verbal assurance or a press release.

    Why it matters. Twelve years from registration to completion is long. Each extension, and whether buyers consented, shows how the project has been run and what your date is worth.

    The original certificate, every extension order and the allottee-consent records.

    "Covid delays" without the orders.

    One date, in writing, matching the agreement and the registration.
